label: copy-phase input t fed back early in recall (sequence starting with t)
explanation: Fires when the letter t comes back in as an input during the copy phase, early in recall: the t was original token 0 or 1 (recall_idx 1-2) and the absolute step is at most 9, so short-to-medium sequences. 99.9% of activation mass is on in_tok = t, and 99.9% is in the copy phase. It is strongest right after <DEL>, at recall_idx 1, when the sequence started with t (80% of mass; top examples are all t x x x <DEL> [t]). It is weaker when t was the second original token (recall_idx 2, 18% of mass), and it fades as L grows, going silent by step 12. It does not fire on t in the original phase, on the delimiter, on t later in recall (recall_idx 4 or higher), or on any other token (a few weak activations on z/e). The output token does not modulate it.

issues: The factual claims hold on the dev profile. In_tok=t carries 99.9% of mass, the copy phase 99.9%, recall_idx 1 80.5%, recall_idx 2 18.5%, recall_idx 3 0.9%, and recall_idx 4 and up is 0. Activations reach 0 by step 12 (step 11 has 9 active steps). The original phase has 158 active steps and z/e about 300 combined, which is scattered noise.
The label slightly overclaims. 'Sequence starting with t' covers only recall_idx 1. The predicate and about 18% of mass also cover t as the second original token (recall_idx 2).

The remaining test false positives (2907) sit almost entirely at step 9, e.g. 'p t i p k v 1 <DEL> p *t*'. This is a soft fade at the step-9 boundary: precision is 0.71 for recall_idx 1 at t=9 and 0.36 for recall_idx 2 at t=9. It is graded decay, not a separate class of inputs.
The test misses (2275 steps, 1.2% of mass) are weak t activations at recall_idx 3 (around 0.01-0.10 of max) plus a few on z. Adding recall_idx 3 lowers F1 (0.82 dev).

The tested alternatives score no higher, apart from one small tweak. Using L in place of t, using a cap of t<=8, or adding conditions on n_seen or out_tok all gave dev F1 0.83-0.87. Excluding (recall_idx==2 & t==9) gives a marginal gain: test F1 0.907 vs 0.896.
